visual: Deep purple young foliage · white bell-shaped flowers · dark red calyces
soilWarning: Acid to neutral soil · shelter from cold winds
prune: Pruning Group 1; prune only if needed after flowering
hardinessNote: RHS H5; foliage colour is strongest in full sun
uses: specimen · city gardens · courtyards · cottage gardens
uncertain: RHS gives 2.5–4 m ultimate height and spread, while Trees and Shrubs Online reports about 2.5–3.5 m after 10 years; RHS dimensions were prioritised for garden planning
The cultivar was discovered as a chance seedling by Henny Kolster in Boskoop in 2001 and was initially known as 'Kolster Purple'; no separate breeder denomination was confirmed
Foliage colour varies with light: full sun maintains the strongest purple coloration, while shade can cause it to fade towards olive green
